data.title: Combined oral contraceptives (in dermatology)
data.summary: Miscellaneous systemic drugs · Oestrogen (ethinylestradiol) + progestin combinations
data.category: More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Oestrogen (ethinylestradiol) + progestin combinations

## Mechanism of action
- Suppress ovarian androgen production (LH suppression), raise sex hormone-binding globulin (less free testosterone), reduce sebum
- Progestins with anti-androgenic action preferred: drospirenone, cyproterone, chlormadinone, dienogest; avoid androgenic progestins (levonorgestrel, norgestrel)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne in women (FDA-approved COCs: drospirenone, norgestimate, norethindrone acetate/ferrous fumarate combinations)
- Hirsutism, PCOS, female pattern hair loss, hidradenitis suppurativa
- Contraception during teratogenic therapy (isotretinoin, acitretin, thalidomide, spironolactone)

## Dose & formulations
- One tablet daily (21/7 or 24/4 regimens); acne improves after 3–6 cycles

## Adverse effects
- Venous thromboembolism (higher with drospirenone/cyproterone than levonorgestrel), stroke/MI (smokers >35)
- Nausea, breast tenderness, breakthrough bleeding, mood change, melasma (can worsen), erythema nodosum, photosensitivity, spider angiomas
- Hypertension

## Contraindications
- Thrombosis history or thrombophilia, smokers over 35, migraine with aura, uncontrolled hypertension, liver disease, oestrogen-dependent cancer, breastfeeding <6 weeks

## Drug interactions
- Enzyme inducers (rifampicin, griseofulvin, carbamazepine, efavirenz) reduce efficacy
- Tetracyclines: no clinically significant reduction (except rifampicin) per current evidence

## Monitoring
- BP, migraine history, smoking status

## Pregnancy & lactation
Stop if pregnant.

## Viva points
- Choose anti-androgenic progestins for acne
- Melasma and erythema nodosum can be caused by COCs
- Rifampicin and griseofulvin reduce efficacy

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.34; Khopkar (Antiandrogens — oral contraceptives). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
